title: The two-sided Bogoliubov inequality in von Neumann algebras conceptualizes the free energy--quantum correlations link
authors: Benedikt M. Reible, Albert Much, Rainer Verch, Christof Schütte, Luigi Delle Site
abstract: The quantum-mechanical two-sided Bogoliubov inequality provides upper and lower bounds for the free energy required to separate a system of interacting particles into independent subsystems. The bounds can be calculated straightforwardly from the ensemble average of the interface energy, bypassing the direct evaluation of the free energy. In this work, we generalize the two-sided Bogoliubov inequality to arbitrary von Neumann algebras by employing the Araki-Uhlmann relative entropy and the framework of unbounded perturbation theory of KMS states. Furthermore, we obtain variational expressions for the relative free energy that extend existing bounded-perturbation principles to the unbounded setting. Crucially, these mathematical developments yield a physically well-founded thermodynamic criterion for the quantification of entanglement in infinite-dimensional systems.
summary: This paper generalizes the two-sided Bogoliubov inequality from finite quantum systems to abstract von Neumann algebras. By employing relative entropy and unbounded perturbation theory, the authors establish rigorous variational bounds for the relative free energy. This provides a mathematically robust, thermodynamically grounded criterion for quantifying entanglement in complex, infinite-dimensional quantum systems.
main_problem: The work aims to generalize the quantum-mechanical two-sided Bogoliubov inequality, which links free energy to quantum correlations, to the abstract setting of von Neumann algebras.
main_result: They establish computable bounds for the relative free energy using generalized inequalities and derive variational expressions that extend bounded-perturbation principles to unbounded systems.
method: The methodology involves advanced mathematical tools from operator algebras, specifically utilizing Araki-Uhlmann relative entropy and the framework of unbounded perturbation theory for KMS states.
model_or_system: The analysis considers general quantum systems described by a von Neumann algebra $M$ with a faithful KMS state $\omega$, modeling interactions via perturbations $U$. The initial physical context involves interacting particles in infinite-dimensional systems, such as those found in quantum field theory.
key_observables: Relative free energy ($F(\omega_U, \omega)$) and the entanglement quantification derived from thermodynamic measurements.
important_parameters: Inverse temperature ($ eta$), interaction strength (related to $U$), and the structure of the von Neumann algebra.
main_assumptions: The generalization relies on assuming the existence of a faithful KMS state $\omega$ and employing advanced mathematical machinery like modular theory.
paper_structure: The paper reviews the known quantum-mechanical inequality, then systematically generalizes it to von Neumann algebras using relative entropy and unbounded perturbation theory. Finally, variational expressions for the relative free energy are derived as a key result.
why_interesting: This work provides rigorous mathematical tools (generalized inequalities) to quantify entanglement in complex, infinite-dimensional systems by framing it within established thermodynamic principles of statistical mechanics.
